title: Monitoring, Alerts, and Logs
summary: Interpret synthetic dashboards, alerts, and logs without confusing evidence with diagnosis.
objectives: Classify synthetic status information as informational, warning, or critical within a defined scenario.
Use timestamps and changing values to describe what happened without claiming an unconfirmed cause.

vocab.def: A message that a condition deserves attention.
A time-ordered record of events or state changes.
A defined point at which a value changes status or requires attention.

sections.heading: Monitoring shows system state
sections.body: Synthetic monitoring may show temperature, utilization, storage, power state, network status, or service status. It gives evidence about conditions at particular times.

sections.heading: Alerts need context
sections.body: Informational, warning, and critical labels are classroom categories for this scenario. A warning says to investigate; it does not prove a root cause.

sections.heading: Read a sequence
sections.body: A log with timestamps can show what changed first. Compare the order of events before deciding what to investigate next.

practice.prompt: A synthetic log shows a temperature warning after a fan-status change. Write two observations and one question without naming a confirmed cause.

quiz.question: What does an alert tell you?
options: That a condition deserves attention and investigation
That the root cause is already known
That a system must be shut down
quiz.answer: That a condition deserves attention and investigation

lab.objective: Read a synthetic dashboard and log sequence, then classify the status and list evidence.

reflectionPrompt: Why is it useful to write down what an alert says before deciding what it means?
